title: Nancy Mace Gets Inked
dek: The outgoing South Carolina congresswoman spent years hiding her tattoos under blazers. Now she's showing both arms off on her own YouTube show, and Republicans can't stop talking about it.
body: Nancy Mace has a new job lined up for after Congress, and a new look to go with it. The three-term South Carolina Republican lost the governor's primary in June, gave up her House seat to make that run, and leaves Washington in January. In August she launched a YouTube talk show called Get Maced. The promo reel showed her sleeveless, with ink running down both arms.

Mace first talked about the tattoos in a February Politico profile. She said she got nine of them fast, in late 2023 and early 2024, during a rough stretch in which her whole congressional staff walked out. She called it "the pain that I need to feel" and said it was a way to reclaim her body.

For months they stayed under her jackets. The August episode put them on camera. Pieces identified so far include the opening line of Virginia Woolf's Mrs Dalloway, the word JUSTICE, a robed saint with a halo, a lion, roses in color and in black and grey, a sun, and a bird on her shoulder that she corrected on X: a hawk, not an eagle.
She has since said the count is well past nine. On TMZ in September she pointed out a swallow and a heart with a "mama" banner, and tied the work to what she called three years of trauma.

Get Maced is a YouTube talk show where Mace takes on the news of the day. In September she hosted an episode in a leather catsuit that the internet immediately called Catwoman, while talking about the Iran war and Michigan's Senate race.

Some on the right were not into it. Mace posted that her biceps should not be a news story, then answered critics on her show. Others in MAGA world said they liked the look. She has hinted the show and her commentary will keep going after she leaves office.
Whatever comes next, it's the rare politician who leaves Congress with more ink than when she arrived, and puts it front and center on her own channel.
